correctness.rationale: The theorem is an exact finite mod-two statement: the supplied standalone program generates all 12 affine lines, all 4096 retained-line families and all 511 nonempty vertex masks for each family. It explicitly builds each mod-two simplicial boundary and computes binary ranks, Euler consistency, all distribution entries, absence of unclaimed homology, both exceptional incidence predicates and acyclicity of their immediate predecessors. Independent oriented-boundary computations over GF(3) and GF(101) agree throughout. The two sphere cases also have direct join/cone proofs. No infinite or integral claims are made; the complete verifier was executed from its actual deliverable path and returned PASS.

originality.rationale: The known full-line homology is expressly credited to Lew (thesis Figure 1.1) and not treated as original. Lew 2020 establishes boxicity and a general duality for partial Steiner systems, but neither paper provides or implies the explicit all-4096 line-erasure Betti distribution, pencil and parallel-class exceptions, or acyclic-to-sphere adjacency statement without a new exhaustive calculation. Gower 1997/1998 addresses defining sets, not homology in its accessible abstract; its full text is a residual access risk. Indexed literature searches for explicit statement, cap-complex aliases, exceptional surviving lines, and block deletions returned no corresponding exact claim; similar affine-plane findings concern distinct incidence graph topologies and cannot determine this table. Prior relevant scientific claims were compared by mathematical implications, not by titles. This is a best-knowledge positive novelty assessment subject to specified access limits, not an independence certificate.
residual_risks: Gower original article full text unavailable; its deeper sections were not verified to exclude a homological-erasure study.

value.rationale: The result completely classifies a canonical finite family of all 4096 partial affine Steiner-line systems, not an arbitrary bounded sample or recomputation of the known full-line complex. It reveals a sharp nonmonotone topological change, with new degree-four sphere homology exactly on nine concurrent-line pencils and degree-five sphere homology exactly on four parallel classes; every immediate one-block predecessor of each exceptional complex is mod-two acyclic. These incidence-geometric distinctions are not visible from the mere number of retained blocks, and give a natural exact robustness invariant for hypergraph independence complexes. The finite statement needs no speculative downstream application to be mathematically motivated.
